Before testing

Authorization controls the technique

Owning a deployed device does not automatically authorize testing a manufacturer’s cloud, a building owner’s system, or a third-party radio network.

  • Written targets, locations and testing window
  • Named escalation contact and stop conditions
  • Separate approval for disruptive or invasive work
  • Spare units and recovery procedure for deep testing

      Methodology

      How this planner was constructed

      The checklist combines recognized IoT testing structures with the operational needs of an enterprise device operator.

      01

      Model the device and attacker

      OWASP ISTG recommends building a device model, defining the attacker perspective, selecting applicable tests, and using stable test identifiers for reproducible reporting.

      02

      Cover chip to cloud

      Professional service catalogs consistently cover hardware, firmware, radio and network communication, companion applications, cloud APIs and the update mechanism.

      03

      Profile to the use case

      NIST’s baseline is a starting point that should be filtered for the device, deployment and organization—not treated as a universal pass/fail certification.

      Primary references

      Professional guides and service catalogs reviewed

      Adaptation note

      Payatu’s public material is oriented toward product makers and deep device testing. This planner preserves that full-stack model while adding enterprise-operator concerns such as inventory accuracy, VLAN segmentation, facilities ownership, vendor remote access, support status and safe production testing.
